dedupe_keys.name: graph based model for reliability analysis of infrastructure networks tum riesgos

description: This model simulates cascading effects within an infrastructure network such as a power grid or water supply system. Its input is the probability of failure of each nodal component, and its output is the estimated probability of service disruption in the areas the network supplies. It includes a taxonomy of network components (nodes and lines) with fragility functions, the conditional probability of failure given an intensity measure, taken from FEMA (2003), and its cascading algorithm follows Crucitti, Latora and Marchiori (2004), Hernandez-Fajardo (2012) and Poljanšek, Bono and Gutiérrez (2012). The script is written in Python with JSON pre- and post-processing files, and the data include an example for the power network of the Valparaíso Region in Chile under earthquake events. It was published by Hugo Rosero-Velásquez at TUM in March 2024 (version 1.0) through mediaTUM with a DataCite DOI, with funding from the German research ministry's RIESGOS and RIESGOS 2.0 projects. Licence: the German open data catalogue lists it as closed, and the mediaTUM page, which holds the files, was not readable from our checks. Caveats: fragility curves are generic literature values and the example is a single region. It supports cascading failure, resilience and earthquake hazard exposure studies of lifeline networks; a related record is the InfraRisk model.
